To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the baroreflex adjusts heart rate to stabilize the double product during spontaneous variations in systolic blood pressure in conscious rabbits.

the product of heart rate and blood pressure power spectra each exhibits a low frequency peak (0.05 Hz) that is associated with high spectral coherence and a negative phase relationship between the two variables (blood pressure leading).

the product of HR and SBP, the double (pressure rate) product, exhibits reduced power at 0.5 Hz when the product is calculated from actual SBP and HR values compared with the product of surrogates of HR and SBPs in which the reflex interactions between HR, SBP, and the double product were removed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the baroreceptor reflex on the heart rate (HR), blood pressure (BP) and their product.
the role of the baroreflex in stabilizing the double product (the product of systolic blood pressure [SBP] and heart rate [HR]) at 0. 05 Hz in conscious, freely moving animals.
the regulation of cardiac oxygen consumption in conscious animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
baroreceptor-mediated reflexes stabilize cardiac work (and oxygen consumption) during spontaneous variations in blood pressure.
the baroreflex stabilizes the DP at low frequencies in rabbits.
the baroreflex stabilizes the DP in the frequency domain, and this is accomplished by the baroreflex adjusting HR so that it is inversely proportional to SBP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the baroreflex stabilizes the double product at 0 Hz and 0.05Hz in rabbits.
baroreflexes stabilize the DP in the frequency region in which the baroreflexes are active.
the baroreflex stabilizes cardiac oxygen consumption during spontaneous fluctuations in arterial pressure in the conscious rabbit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the baroreflex can be used to stabilize the double product in rabbits, and possibly other species.
the double product (product of heart rate and systolic blood) is not a reliable measure of oxygen demand in the presence of baroreflexes.

baroreflex stabilization of HR and the double product is not due to a reflex interaction between the two variables, but instead is the result of the baroreflex adjusting HR to stabilize the double product.
